title: Krateo PlatformOps Installer
description: Umbrella orchestrator. Create one Installer Composition per Krateo platform installation. It registers and emits the component blueprints in dependency order. Pinned to installer 2.7.0.

global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)

bootstrap.title: Bootstrap (composition engine)
bootstrap.description: When true, install core-provider as a conditional subchart dependency (gated by bootstrap.coreProvider.enabled) so a bare-cluster helm install self-bootstraps. The hook-weighting that orders bootstrap is on the installer's own self-bootstrap Job, not the subchart.

waitForSynced.description: When true, the bootstrap adds a final hook wave that blocks until the Installer CR is Synced (honest `deployed`), at the cost of a longer client-interruption window. Off by default.

exposure.title: Exposure
exposure.description: Exposure model for browser-facing components. LoadBalancer/NodePort set spec.service.type and are resolved via Helm lookup at reconcile time; Gateway keeps Services ClusterIP and emits one Gateway API HTTPRoute per exposed component, attached to a BYO Gateway.

port.title: Exposure port
port.description: Optional. Overrides the single port browser-facing (expose:true, top-level Service) components are exposed on — sets both their Service port and the frontend config.json peer URLs (http://<lb-ip>:<port>). Unset => each component keeps its per-component exposePort default. Nested-Service (kagent) and own-LB (hyperdx) components are set via componentValues. Ignored when type=Gateway (routing is by hostname).

gatewayRef.title: Gateway reference (type=Gateway)
gatewayRef.description: The Gateway API Gateway the emitted HTTPRoutes attach to (parentRef). BYO / agentgateway — the installer does NOT create the Gateway or its CRDs. Required when type=Gateway.

baseDomain.title: Base domain (type=Gateway)
baseDomain.description: Per-component hostnames are derived as <svcMatch>.<baseDomain> (authn.<baseDomain>, snowplow.<baseDomain>, ...). Override any single host via exposure.hosts.<component-name>. Used only when type=Gateway; the frontend config peer URLs become https://<host>.

hosts.title: Per-component hostname overrides (type=Gateway)
hosts.description: Explicit hostname per component name (keys are component names, e.g. frontend), overriding the <svcMatch>.<baseDomain> derivation. Use for the frontend (e.g. portal.<domain> or the apex) or any component that shouldn't follow the derived pattern.

coreProvider.description: Engine-present marker (core-provider is always-on via bootstrap). Gates no component.

coreAgents.description: Deploy the base agent layer: kagent-crds -> kagent -> model-configs (the kagent ModelConfigs the whole fleet references by name) + installer-agent + krateo-autopilot (which also brings up repo-mcp-server, the fleet's grounding server) + incident-agent (alert root-cause analysis). Default false.

portal.description: The non-agent platform: authn/snowplow/frontend/portal + portal-starter + the observability stack (operators, krateo-observability, otel collectors, sse-proxy the portal's events bell consumes).

oasgenProvider.description: Deploy oasgen-provider (generates operators from OpenAPI specs).

specialistAgents.description: Deploy the 5 component specialist agents (authn/snowplow/frontend/clickstack/core-provider) + clickhouse-mcp (needs coreAgents).

ingress.description: Opt-in edge layer: ExternalDNS (DNS record publication) + cert-manager-issuers (ACME certificate issuance) from oci://ghcr.io/krateo-blueprints/charts. Default false — the base install is unchanged and pulls nothing from krateo-blueprints unless enabled. Turn off if you run behind your own ingress controller / cloud LB / mesh, or manage DNS+certs yourself. Preconditions when enabled: ExternalDNS needs its provider-credential Secret placed out-of-band (referenced by the component's secretRef); cert-manager-issuers' ACME HTTP-01 solver assumes the Gateway API edge is present.

codegenAgents.description: Opt-in codegen/conversion specialist agents (code-analysis, ansible-to-operator, tf-provider-to-operator, tf-to-helm) from krateo-agentiko/codegen-agents. Needs coreAgents. Default false.

agentGateway.description: Opt-in agent gateway: an agentgateway data plane in front of the kagent fleet (components agentgateway-controller + agentgateway-policies, from oci://ghcr.io/krateo-agentiko/charts), giving JWT authentication and per-user RBAC over which agent a caller may reach, which MCP tools it may run and which sub-agents it may delegate to. A valid token becomes mandatory on every agent endpoint, so it never turns on through an upgrade. Needs coreAgents and an issuer whose JWKS the gateway trusts (authn, via portal, by default). Every setting is the policies chart's own: componentValues.agentgateway-policies.

components.title: Component DAG (advanced override)
components.description: Advanced. Each entry, matched by `name`, either OVERRIDES a pinned component (whitelisted fields: version / repo / chart / registerOnly / tier — e.g. registerOnly:true to demote a pinned component to registered-but-not-installed, installer#38; or `repo` (+ `chart` for a differing artifact name) to pull that component's chart from a DIFFERENT registry so the source need not be equal for all components, installer#84 — for a re-source to a different registry use registryAuth.registries[] mode so the override gets its OWN pull credential, not the global one) or APPENDS a new registerOnly catalog blueprint. Only `name` is required — an override needs just the field it changes; an append needs kind+version (enforced at render).

repo.description: OCI registry base overriding ociRepo for this component's chart URL.

chart.description: Chart artifact name overriding the component name in the OCI URL (e.g. krateo-snowplow). The component name stays the CompositionDefinition/Composition identity; only the chart path changes.

chartRepo.description: CompositionDefinition spec.chart.repo — classic helm repo NAME (only for non-OCI helm-repo charts; OCI components don't need it).

serviceValuesPath.description: Dotted path to the component chart's Service values block when it is NOT the chart top-level `service` (e.g. kagent's UI Service lives at `kagentapp.ui.service`). The exposure layer builds this nested path and sets `.type` = .Values.exposure.type, flipping the right Service to LoadBalancer/NodePort while the component chart keeps its default.

internalUrls.description: Internal (ClusterIP) URLs this component's chart hardcodes at a peer's per-component default port — e.g. snowplow's env.URL_AUTHN, sse-proxy's auth.urlAuthn. When exposure.port collapses the browser-facing Services onto one shared port those hardcoded ports go dead, so compositions.yaml recomputes each URL on the shared port.

path.description: Dotted path in the component chart's values to overwrite.

peer.description: Service name of the peer the URL points at.

internalPorts.description: Port-only sibling of internalUrls: an INTEGER port the chart hardcodes at an exposed peer's default — e.g. agentgateway-policies' jwt.jwks.port. Recomputed to exposure.port under the same gate.

path.description: Dotted path in the component chart's values to overwrite.

frontendConfigEnv.description: Opt-in: env var key to inject into this component's spec.env with the frontend config-vars ConfigMap name, COMPUTED from the consumer (frontend) component (see compositions.yaml). Used by snowplow's Phase-1 nav-prewarm walker.

agent.description: This component DEPLOYS a kagent Agent. Drives four things at once: the .vertexAI injection (the pod's ADC env / SA-key mount), the HITL approval gate, agentgateway.enabled, and membership of the orchestrator's auto-derived extraAgents fleet. Not set on model-configs, which renders ModelConfigs but no Agent — see modelOwner.

modelOwner.description: This component OWNS the shared ModelConfigs the rest of the fleet references (model-configs). It is NOT an `agent` (it deploys no Agent), but takes the same .vertexAI injection and agentgateway.enabled, plus the .localModel injection and the agentgateway LLM-route wiring that are its alone. Distinct from `orchestrator` — owning the fleet's models and orchestrating the fleet are different jobs on different components.

requireApproval.description: GRANULAR kagent HITL override (compositions.yaml): the exact list of this agent's tool names that pause for human approval. When present it is threaded onto the agent's spec verbatim and the coarse global .hitlApproval boolean is NOT applied to this agent. Use [] for an agent whose only mutating-shaped tool is a NON-mutating validator (e.g. frontend-agent's k8s_apply_manifest server dry-run) so its authoring loop is not gated — the real write gate stays downstream (publishPage blast-radius). Omit the key entirely for agents that should inherit the coarse global gate on their own mutating tools.

registerOnly.description: Catalog blueprint: Pass A registers this component's CompositionDefinition (making the blueprint available in the portal) but Pass B never emits a Composition for it — the operator/end-user instantiates it on demand. Use for tenant workload blueprints (e.g. openstack) that ship in the catalog rather than being auto-installed. Typically paired with tier: catalog.

nodePort.description: Pinned NodePort for a browser-facing (expose:true) component when exposure.type=NodePort — deterministic + host-mappable. Wired to spec.service.nodePort in composition mode.

resources.description: Per-Kind CDC controller compute resources (corev1.ResourceRequirements), threaded onto the component CompositionDefinition spec.resources. Absent -> the core-provider chart cdc.resources default applies.

orchestrator.description: This agent is the fleet's ORCHESTRATOR (krateo-autopilot): it auto-attaches every deployed, feature-enabled `agent` component as an A2A sub-agent via extraAgents. Split out of modelOwner, which now marks the ModelConfig owner instead.

localModel.title: Local LLM (Ollama)
localModel.description: Opt-in (off by default). Run the whole agent fleet on one local Ollama model instead of Gemini/Vertex. The modelOwner component renders every model slot as provider Ollama at host, so every agent referencing a slot follows with no per-agent change. Use a tool-calling-capable model (qwen3.6 recommended).

model.description: Local model id pulled in Ollama; must support tool calling.

vertexAI.title: Gemini Vertex AI
vertexAI.description: Vertex AI for the autopilot agents via Application Default Credentials (no API key). Requires the GKE node SA to have aiplatform access and the cloud-platform OAuth scope.

secretName.title: Vertex SA-key Secret name
secretName.description: k8s Secret with the GCP service-account key JSON for portable explicit-key ADC (any cluster). Unset => metadata-server ADC (GKE node SA).

secretKey.title: Key file inside the Secret
secretKey.description: File name inside secretName; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/var/secrets/gcp/<secretKey>. Default key.json.

hitlApproval.title: HITL approval
hitlApproval.description: Human-in-the-loop approval gate applied to every vertexAI agent (autopilot orchestrator + subagents): true pauses each mutating tool call for chat approval; false runs autonomously.

componentValues.title: Per-component spec overrides
componentValues.description: Per-component Composition spec overrides, STRICTLY TYPED against each pinned component's chart schema. This is a HAND-CURATED, deliberate override surface: every leaf is explicitly typed and unknown keys are REJECTED (additionalProperties is false on every object). No free-form escapes remain anywhere in this schema (neither an open additionalProperties nor the k8s preserve-unknown extension) — enforced in CI by .github/workflows/check-no-unknowns.yaml. Invariants: each component's `global` is the fixed engine-injected block (plumbing InjectGlobalValues) plus imageRegistry; `resources` is k8s ResourceRequirements (limits/requests each with cpu/memory); label, annotation and nodeSelector maps are typed string maps. To expose a NEW override knob for a component, add it here explicitly and typed — do not reintroduce a free-form object. Deep-merged into the rendered Composition spec; the installer-computed wiring (service.type/config/vertexAI/hitlApproval) stays authoritative and wins on any leaf conflict.

chartGate.description: The render-and-validate gate the agent chart deploys (Deployment + Service + RemoteMCPServer): helm lint --strict, flux schema validate with CEL, kube-linter. A blueprint is finished only when it returns ok=true.

url.description: Empty means the agent chart's own Service. Set it to use a gate deployed elsewhere.

replicaCount.description: Keep at 1: Streamable-HTTP MCP sessions are stateful, so a second replica breaks follow-up calls with "400 No valid session ID provided".

tag.description: Empty means the agent chart version, so chart X.Y.Z asks for image X.Y.Z.

iterationCap.description: How many times the agent may re-run the gate on one chart before it stops and reports what still fails. Stamped into the prompt.

gateTimeoutSeconds.description: The gate's own per-call limit. Keep it below `timeout` so an overrun reaches the agent as a JSON envelope rather than a transport error.

liveDryRun.description: The gate's last validating step: submit every rendered document to this cluster's API server with `kubectl create --dry-run=server`, so the operators' validating webhooks judge it. Nothing is persisted. A kind whose operator is not installed is reported as `operatorMissing` and does NOT fail the chart.

create.description: Render the ClusterRole (`create` on `*`) + binding the dry-run needs. A blueprint can render any kind, so the grant cannot be enumerated, and RBAC has no dry-run-only verb. `false` to bind your own narrower role: a Forbidden is reported as not-checked, never as a chart defect.

perDocumentTimeoutSeconds.description: Per-document kubectl timeout, so one slow admission webhook cannot consume the whole step.

budgetSeconds.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole step. Keep it below `gateTimeoutSeconds` with room for the earlier steps: spending it yields a readable partial report naming the documents never reached, where overrunning the server's per-call limit would throw the whole envelope away.

maxDocuments.description: Ceiling on documents submitted per call, so a large chart cannot exhaust `gateTimeoutSeconds`. Whatever is dropped is named in the report.

items.description:
The pod this Toleration is attached to tolerates any taint that matches
the triple <key,value,effect> using the matching operator <operator>.

effect.description:
Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects.
When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute.

key.description:
Key is the taint key that the toleration applies to. Empty means match all taint keys.
If the key is empty, operator must be Exists; this combination means to match all values and all keys.

operator.description:
Operator represents a key's relationship to the value.
Valid operators are Exists, Equal, Lt, and Gt. Defaults to Equal.
Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a pod can
tolerate all taints of a particular category.
Lt and Gt perform numeric comparisons (requires feature gate TaintTolerationComparisonOperators).

tolerationSeconds.description:
TolerationSeconds represents the period of time the toleration (which must be
of effect NoExecute, otherwise this field is ignored) tolerates the taint. By default,
it is not set, which means tolerate the taint forever (do not evict). Zero and
negative values will be treated as 0 (evict immediately) by the system.

value.description:
Value is the taint value the toleration matches to.
If the operator is Exists, the value should be empty, otherwise just a regular string.

dataSource.description:
dataSource field can be used to specify either:
* An existing VolumeSnapshot object (snapshot.storage.k8s.io/VolumeSnapshot)
* An existing PVC (PersistentVolumeClaim)
If the provisioner or an external controller can support the specified data source,
it will create a new volume based on the contents of the specified data source.
When the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate is enabled, dataSource contents will be copied to dataSourceRef,
and dataSourceRef contents will be copied to dataSource when dataSourceRef.namespace is not specified.
If the namespace is specified, then dataSourceRef will not be copied to dataSource.

apiGroup.description:
APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced.
If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.

kind.description: Kind is the type of resource being referenced

name.description: Name is the name of resource being referenced

dataSourceRef.description:
dataSourceRef specifies the object from which to populate the volume with data, if a non-empty
volume is desired. This may be any object from a non-empty API group (non
core object) or a PersistentVolumeClaim object.
When this field is specified, volume binding will only succeed if the type of
the specified object matches some installed volume populator or dynamic
provisioner.
This field will replace the functionality of the dataSource field and as such
if both fields are non-empty, they must have the same value. For backwards
compatibility, when namespace isn't specified in dataSourceRef,
both fields (dataSource and dataSourceRef) will be set to the same
value automatically if one of them is empty and the other is non-empty.
When namespace is specified in dataSourceRef,
dataSource isn't set to the same value and must be empty.
There are three important differences between dataSource and dataSourceRef:
* While dataSource only allows two specific types of objects, dataSourceRef
  allows any non-core object, as well as PersistentVolumeClaim objects.
* While dataSource ignores disallowed values (dropping them), dataSourceRef
  preserves all values, and generates an error if a disallowed value is
  specified.
* While dataSource only allows local objects, dataSourceRef allows objects
  in any namespaces.
(Beta) Using this field requires the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.
(Alpha) Using the namespace field of dataSourceRef requires the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource feature gate to be enabled.

enabled.description: Render the JWT authentication policy and the token-passthrough policy.

mode.description: Strict = no token is a 401, and each sub-agent route gets its own route-scoped Optional policy so the tokenless agent-card fetch still lands. issuer.description: Must equal the token's iss claim (authn: krateo.io).

audiences.description: Allowed aud values. MUST stay empty for authn, which emits no aud claim.

userClaim.description: Claim carrying the user identity (authn: sub).

groupsClaim.description: Claim carrying the group list (authn: groups).

namespace.description: Its namespace. Empty = release namespace; anything else also renders a ReferenceGrant.

cacheDuration.description: How long a fetched JWKS is reused. agentgateway rejects anything below 5m.

cors.description: CORS for the gateway. Only needed when a BROWSER calls it directly (the Krateo portal's Autopilot rail does): the browser sends an unauthenticated OPTIONS preflight first, which the authorization policy would 403, and refuses the real request unless the answer carries Access-Control-Allow-*. Short-circuits the preflight ONLY — a real request with no/bad token is still 403/401. Server-to-server callers are unaffected. The Krateo installer enables it with features.agentGateway.

allowOrigins.description: Origins allowed to call the gateway from a browser. Defaults to '*' because the portal's browser-facing origin is not knowable in-cluster; pin it to the real portal origin when you know it. Safe by default only while allowCredentials is false — the credential is a Bearer header the page must set itself, not a cookie.

allowCredentials.description: Leave false: no cookies are involved, and true alongside allowOrigins ['*'] is rejected by browsers.

maxAge.description: Seconds a browser may cache the preflight answer.

enabled.description: Render the Gateway-level Allow policy carrying layers 1 and 3. false leaves the gateway authenticating without authorizing.

endpointRules.description: Layer 1 — which subjects may reach which agent's A2A endpoint directly.

agents.description: Agent names, or ["*"] for the whole /api/a2a/<ns>/ prefix.

subjects.description: Who a rule grants access to. The matchers are OR'd; at least one must be set, otherwise the rule would deny everyone. `anyAuthenticated` is IGNORED when `users` or `groups` is set: these blocks are deep-merged maps, so a caller narrowing a rule to a group never sees the default `anyAuthenticated: true` disappear, and OR'ing it back in would silently restore access to everyone. Widen again with `anyAuthenticated: true` and no users/groups.

anyAuthenticated.description: Any request carrying a token this gateway validated. Ignored when `users` or `groups` is set.

users.description: Values of the user claim (authn: the username in `sub`).

groups.description: Values that must appear in the groups claim (authn: `groups`, a list of strings).

mcpTraffic.description: Traffic-layer gate for the proxied /mcp hop. Which tool may run is mcpServers[].toolRules.

model-configs.description: The chart that OWNS the fleet's kagent ModelConfigs (one per `models` slot). Every agent references a slot by name, so a model pin, a provider switch or the gateway LLM route is set here once for the whole fleet. Renders no pods.

name.description: ModelConfig object name — what the agents reference. Renaming it means also updating the componentValues.<agent>.modelConfig.name entries that point at it; the names are literals, not aliases resolved for you.

models.description: Model slots this component owns, keyed by an arbitrary alias — one ModelConfig each. The component pins' `model:` field names an alias here.

geminiApiKey.description: Reference to an existing Secret holding the Gemini API key — the default path (no gateway route, no localModel, vertexAI off).

vertexAI.description: Gemini Vertex AI provider for the rendered ModelConfigs (GeminiVertexAI via ADC). Set for you from the umbrella .vertexAI.

localModel.description: Local LLM (Ollama). Set for you from the umbrella .localModel; takes precedence over vertexAI so every slot renders as Ollama.

enabled.description: A gateway exists in this install. Set for you when features.agentGateway is on. This component renders no pods, so here it only selects the default for modelRoute.

Tri-state — LEAVE UNSET unless you mean to override the derivation (on when agentgateway.enabled, off on a localModel install). true forces the route on for a localModel install, which needs the policies chart's llm.custom provider pointed at that same Ollama. false forces it off, which is REQUIRED when you set componentValues.agentgateway-policies.llm.enabled=false — that Gateway carries no LLM route, so routing there 404s every model call.

url.description: Empty = derived from the gateway defaults. The installer fills it only when agentgateway-policies' gateway.name / gateway.port / llm.routePrefix, or namespaces.krateo, are non-default. kagent appends /chat/completions.

apiKeySecret.description: Empty = Passthrough: the caller's own token becomes the LLM credential (apiKeyPassthrough), so no provider key lives in any agent. Set to a Secret holding a shared key — matching componentValues.agentgateway-policies.llm.callerAuth.apiKey.secretRef — for callers that are not user-driven (cron, webhooks) and have no token to forward.

modelRoute.description: Point the fleet's ModelConfigs at the gateway's LLM route instead of straight at the provider (provider OpenAI + openAI.baseUrl). This is what makes anything attached to that route act at all — guardrails, rate limits, token budgets, cost controls. TAKES PRECEDENCE over vertexAI and localModel.

agentgateway.description: The agentgateway in front of the fleet, as it concerns the fleet's models.

global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)
global.description: Context keys the composition-dynamic-controller injects when this chart installs as a component (plumbing InjectGlobalValues), plus the helm-standard imageRegistry override.

registryAuth.title: Private registry credentials
registryAuth.description: When enabled, every component CompositionDefinition (and the installer's own) gets spec.chart.credentials so core-provider can pull charts from a private/authenticated OCI registry in-cluster.

passwordRef.description: Reference to a Secret holding the registry password/token.

imagePullSecretName.description: IMAGE-pull, not just chart-pull. The installer derives a dockerconfigjson Secret from the same registryAuth token(s) and injects it into the components shipping private krateo-agentiko images (autopilot's repo-mcp-server, core-provider-agent's chart-gate-mcp-server, agentgateway-policies' native-RBAC decider), so a full-fleet install needs no manual ServiceAccount patch. Works in BOTH global mode (the top-level token) and registries[] mode (the entry matching each component's repo, so the image-pull token is exactly the one that authorizes that registry). Empty auto-derives (Secret name krateo-registry-image-pull); set to the name of a pre-existing dockerconfigjson Secret in namespaces.krateo to supply your own.

insecureSkipVerifyTLS.description: Skip TLS verification on the in-cluster chart pull (maps to CompositionDefinition spec.chart.insecureSkipVerifyTLS). Applies to every component (a coarse dev toggle), independent of auth; a registries[] entry may raise it for its own registry.

registries.description: Registry-keyed credentials for multi-registry installs. When NON-EMPTY, each component's chart-pull credentials are selected by matching its effective registry base (its `repo` override, else `ociRepo`) against these entries: a matched component gets that entry's credentials; a component whose registry has no entry gets NO credentials, so a token is never presented to a registry it does not belong to. In this mode the global username/passwordRef above are ignored. When EMPTY (default), the legacy global credentials apply to every component unchanged.

repo.description: The OCI registry base this credential authenticates, matched verbatim against a component's effective repo (its `repo` override, else `ociRepo`). e.g. oci://ghcr.io/krateo-agentiko/charts

passwordRef.description: Reference to a Secret holding this registry's password/token.

insecureSkipVerifyTLS.description: Skip TLS verification for pulls from this registry (overrides the global toggle upward for this repo only).
